title: Final Decision C25-0038 2025-FT44 HURRICANE KAZAN - SINGH (APR)
text:
DECISION of the FEI TRIBUNAL
16 February 2026
In the matter of
Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh (APR; Ref. C25-0038)
(FEI Case number: 2025/FT44 HURRICANE KAZAN)
FEI Tribunal Hearing Panel: Mr Brian Ward (CAN)
FEI Tribunal Reference: C25-0038 [FEI 2025/FT44 HURRICANE KAZAN]
Person Responsible/ID/NF: Isa Hameed Dakheel AL ANEZI/10184336/BRN(UAE)
Horse/ID/NF: HURRICANE KAZAN/108LI88/BRN
Trainer/ID/NF: Bhur Singh Ladhu SINGH/10063972/IND(BRN)
Event/Date: CH-M-YH-E 120 8 YO - Jullianges (FRA), 01-02.08.2025
Event ID: 2025_CH-M-YH_0003_E_YH_01
Date of sample collection: 01.08.2025
Prohibited Substance(s): Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate
Bar Code Nos.: 1670598

I. Introduction
1. The Fédération Équestre Internationale (the FEI) alleges that Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh
committed a violation of Article 2.1 of the Equine Anti-Doping & Controlled Medication
Rules – The Presence of a Banned Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a Horse’s
Sample. The FEI notified Mr Singh of the alleged charge in his capacity as the Additional
Person Responsible.
2. Applicable Rules Provisions:
▪ Statutes 25th edition, effective 21 November 2023 (Statutes).
▪ General Regulations, 24th edition, updates effective 1 January 2025 (GRs).
▪ Internal Regulations of the FEI Tribunal, 4th Edition, 1 February 2025 (IRs).
▪ FEI’s Equine Anti-Doping and Controlled Medication Rules, 4th Edition, updates
effective 1 January 2025 (EADCMRs).
▪ FEI’s 2025 Equine Prohibited Substances List (Equine Prohibited List)
3. All the words used in this Decision beginning with a capital letter and not previously
defined have the meaning set forth in the specific definitions of the Statutes, GRs, IRs, the
Equine Prohibited List and the EADCMRs. The Equine Anti-Doping Rules (the EAD Rules)
and the Equine Controlled Medication Rules (the ECM Rules) are set out in the EADCMRs.
II. Factual background
4. Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh (FEI ID 10063972), was the registered trainer (the Additional
Person Responsible or the APR) of the horse Hurricane Kazan (FEI ID 108LI88, the Horse),
which competed in the CH-M-YH-E 120 8 YO – Jullianges, France held on 1 and 2 August
2025 (the Event).
5. The FEI (together with the APR, the Parties), is the sole IOC recognised international
federation for equestrian sport. The FEI is the governing body of the FEI equestrian
disciplines of dressage, jumping, eventing, driving, endurance, vaulting, and para-
equestrian.
6. Blood and urine samples were collected from the Horse on 1 August 2025. The Horse’s
urine sample returned a positive finding for Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate.
2

7. Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate is a corticosteroid used in the treatment of severe allergic
reactions, endocrine and skin disorders. It is the hemisuccinate salt form of
Hydrocortisone and is thus of similar chemical structure and biological effect. It is
classified as a Controlled Medication Substance under the 2025 FEI Equine Prohibited
Substances List.
III. Procedural background
8. On 4 September 2025, the FEI informed the APR of a possible violation of Article 2.1 of
the ECM Rules (the Notification Letter).
9. Despite a reminder sent by the FEI to the APR via the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI)
and the Bahrain Royal Equestrian Federation (BEF), he did not submit a position nor did
he request the analysis of the B Sample. The B Sample was in any case requested by the
PR and the Owner of the Horse.
10. On 14 October 2025, the FEI informed the PR and the Owner of the Horse that the
analysis of the B Sample confirmed the presence of Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate.
11. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted its response and the case file (the FEI’s
Response) to the Tribunal for adjudication.
12. On 19 December 2025, the Tribunal Chair appointed a one-person Hearing Panel to
decide this case. The Parties were asked to provide any objections to the constitution of
the Hearing Panel by 8 January 2025. In addition, the APR was invited to respond to the
FEI’s allegations by submitting a statement of defence and any supporting evidence by
26 January 2026. Finally, the Tribunal Chair informed the Parties of their right to request
a hearing by 28 January 2026, at the latest.
13. The BEF confirmed to the Tribunal that the APR was provided a copy of the Notification
Letter and no response was received from the APR.
IV. The Parties’ Submissions:1
A. Submissions by the APR
14. The APR elected to not submit any position.
1 The following section is a summary of the relevant facts and evidence of the FEI’s written submission.
3

B. Submissions by the FEI:
15. On 15 December 2025, the FEI submitted the FEI Response to the Tribunal. The FEI’s
position is summarised as follows:
15.1 Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules prohibits the presence of a Controlled Medication
Substance and/or its Metabolites or Markers in a horse's sample. As a strict
liability offence, it is not necessary that intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use
be demonstrated in order to establish an ECM Rule violation under Article 2.1.
15.2 In the present case, the analysis of the Sample confirmed the presence of
Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate in the Horse’s system. This finding alone satisfies
the requirements of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
15.3 Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules provides that an Additional Person Responsible with
no previous ECM Rule violation, but who violates Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules, is
subject to a period of Ineligibility of six (6) months, unless he can rebut the
presumption of Fault on a balance of probability.
15.4 Therefore, in this case, to rebut the presumption of Fault, the APR must establish
to the satisfaction of the Tribunal (on a balance of probability), how the
Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate entered the Horse’s system. The APR must also
demonstrate one of the following:
1. He bears No Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, i.e., that he did not
know or suspect, and could not reasonably have known or suspected even
with the exercise of utmost caution, that he had administered to the horse
(or the horse’s system otherwise contained) a Banned Substance. If proven,
the period of Ineligibility is eliminated completely pursuant to Article 10.5 of
the ECM Rules.
2. He bears No Significant Fault or Negligence for that occurrence, in which
case, the period of Ineligibility may be reduced based on the degree of fault,
pursuant to Article 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
15.5 The FEI submitted that since the APR failed to reply to the charges, he did not
establish how the Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate entered the Horse’s body, and it
is therefore not possible to evaluate his level of Fault or Negligence, if any, pursuant
to the applicable rules. As a consequence, the presumption of Fault as stipulated
in the Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules shall stand.
4

15.6 The FEI also stated that no elimination or reduction of the period of Ineligibility in
this case is possible and the applicable sanction for the current violation should be
6 (six) months of Ineligibility in accordance with Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules
15.7 The FEI respectfully requested that the Tribunal issue a decision:
(i) upholding the charge that the APR has violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules;
(ii) imposing a period of Ineligibility of six (6) months on the APR, commencing from
the date of the Final Decision pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules;
(iii) fining the APR in the amount of 3’500 CHF (three thousand five hundred);
(iv) ordering the APR to pay the legal costs of 2’000 CHF (two thousand) that the FEI
has incurred in these proceedings.
V. Legal Analysis
A. Jurisdiction
16. The Tribunal has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to Article 38 of the Statutes, Article
161 of the GRs, Article 8 of the ECM Rules and Article 18 of the IRs. The APR is a member
of the EFI and the BEF, which are both members of the FEI; therefore, the APR is bound
by the ECM Rules.
B. Legal Discussion
17. Although the Tribunal has fully considered all the facts, legal arguments and evidence in
the present proceedings, it refers only to the facts and evidence it considers necessary
to explain its reasoning in this decision.
i. The Burden of Proof
18. Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules states that sufficient proof of a violation is established by the
presence of a Controlled Medication Substance in a horse’s sample. The Tribunal is satisfied
that the laboratory report on the Sample reflects that the analytical tests were performed
in an acceptable manner and that the findings are accurate. The Tribunal is further satisfied
that the test results evidence the presence of Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate in the Sample
taken from the Horse at the Event. Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate is a Controlled
Medication Substance and the presence of this substance in a horse’s system is prohibited
at all times under Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
5

19. Pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules, the FEI bears the burden to establish all of the
elements of the ECM Rule violation to the comfortable satisfaction of the Tribunal. The
Tribunal notes that it is not in dispute that the FEI had successfully established that the
APR committed an ECM Rule violation. As a strict liability offence, it is not necessary to
prove intent, Fault, negligence or knowing Use.
20. The burden of proof then shifts to the APR. The standard of proof for the APR to establish
how the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system is by a balance of probability,
pursuant to Article 3.1 of the ECM Rules. It is not disputed by the Parties that for the APR
to escape a six (6) month sanction, he must establish, on a balance of probability: (i) how
the Prohibited Substance entered the Horse’s system; and (ii) he bears No (Significant)
Fault or Negligence pursuant to Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
ii. Anti-Doping Rule Violation
21. As mentioned above, the violation of Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules is not in dispute. The
analysis of the Samples revealed the presence of Hydrocortisone hemisuccinate in the
Horse’s system, which constitutes sufficient proof of the violation of Article 2.1. Therefore,
the FEI satisfied its burden to establish the ECM Rule violation and sufficiently proved the
objective elements of the violation pursuant to Article 3 of the ECM Rules.
iii. Elimination or Reduction of the Period of Ineligibility
22. Pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules, the period of Ineligibility for an Article 2.1
violation is six (6) months, subject to a potential reduction for No (or No Significant) Fault
or Negligence in accordance with Articles 10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules. To benefit from
a reduction, the APR must establish as a threshold requirement how the Prohibited
Substance entered the Horse’s system.2
23. The APR chose not to participate in the proceedings. Therefore, the Tribunal finds that
the APR did not discharge his burden of proving how the Prohibited Substance entered
the Horse’s system.
24. Where this first hurdle has not been met (i.e., establishing the source of the Prohibited
Substance), the Tribunal cannot continue with the second step and evaluate the APR’s
degree of Fault or Negligence. Consequently, the Tribunal finds that the APR is not
2 FEI Tribunal Decisions: C23-0031 [FEI 2023/FT12 – ALASOUF] dated 12 October 2023, C23-0034 [FEI 2023/CM05
– SAHM II] dated 8 September 2023, C23-0045 [FEI 2023/FT24 – DIFF LOOK] dated 2 November 2023, C23-0046
[2023/CM08 BALLON PARIS] dated 6 December 2023.
6

entitled to any reduction of the otherwise applicable period of Ineligibility under Articles
10.5 or 10.6 of the ECM Rules.
iv. Sanctions
25. As the threshold of source has not been proven, the Tribunal finds that the applicable
period of Ineligibility is six (6) months pursuant to Article 10.2 of the ECM Rules which
shall commence on the date of this decision.
26. The Tribunal also deems that the APR shall pay a fine of CHF 3,500 and pay CHF 2’000 to
the FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
VI. Terms of the Decision
27. As a result, the Panel makes the following decision and imposes the following sanctions
in accordance with Article 164.11 of the GRs and Article 10 of the ECM Rules:
a) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh violated Article 2.1 of the ECM Rules.
b) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh is suspended for a period of six (6) months. The period
of the Ineligibility will be effective from the date of this decision.
c) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh is ordered to pay a fine of three thousand five hundred
Swiss Francs (CHF 3,500).
d) Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh is ordered to pay two thousand Swiss francs (2’000 CHF)
to the FEI as contribution to its legal costs.
28. Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh, the Equestrian Federation of India, the Bahrain Royal
Equestrian Federation and the FEI will be notified this Decision. The Bahrain Royal
Equestrian Federation is requested to immediately transmit and notify the Decision to
Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh.
29. Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh may not, during the period of Ineligibility, participate in any
capacity in a Competition or activity that is authorised or organised by the FEI or any
National Federation or be present at an event (other than as a spectator) that is
authorized or organised by the FEI or any National Federation, or participate in any
capacity in Competitions authorised or organized by any international or national-level
event organisation (Article 10.13.1 of the ECM Rules).
7

30. If Mr Bhur Singh Ladhu Singh violates any of the conditions in the previous paragraph
during the period of Ineligibility, the results of any such participation will be disqualified
and a new period of Ineligibility equal in length up to the original period of Ineligibility will
be added to the end of the original period of Ineligibility. In addition, further sanctions
may be imposed if appropriate (Article 10.13.3 of the ECM Rules).
31. According to Article 170 of the GRs, this Tribunal Decision is effective from the day of
written notification to the persons and bodies concerned.
VII. Legal Action
32. In accordance with Article 12 of the ECM Rules the Parties may appeal this Tribunal
Decision before the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) within twenty-one (21) days of
the present notification.
FOR THE TRIBUNAL
________________________________________
Mr Brian Ward, Sole Panel Member
